reconcile.connective: JFB distinguishes "tempted" as sinful solicitation from "tempted" as mere trial or testing, the distinction harmonizers apply to Christ's wilderness temptation.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells presses the flat wording: James denies God can be tempted, yet Jesus plainly was — proof, he argues, that Jesus isn't God.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Is Jesus God?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/Jesus_God.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: when . . . tempted--tried by solicitation to evil. Heretofore the "temptation" meant was that of probation by afflictions. … God is said in Gen 22:1 to have "tempted Abraham"; but there the tempting meant is that of trying or proving, not that of seducement.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: JFB explicitly distinguishes two senses of 'tempted' in James 1:13 — solicitation to evil (excluded from God) vs. trial/testing (used of God 'tempting' Abraham, Gen 22:1) — the exact semantic move harmonizers use to argue Jesus's temptation (Heb 4:15/Matt 4, the trial sense) does not fall under James's denial (the solicitation sense).

link.title: CARM: God cannot be tempted. Jesus was tempted. Therefore, Jesus cannot be God.
link.note: Live apologetics page devoted specifically to this contradiction; argues the resolution turns on the (scripturally underspecified) relation between Christ's divine and human natures.
